stem: the Devi Mahatmya, also called the Chandi or the Durga Saptashati, is traditionally found inside which larger text?
options: the Brahmanda Purana
the Markandeya Purana
the Bhagavata Purana
the Shiva Purana
why: The Devi Mahatmya is a block of thirteen chapters in the Markandeya Purana (chapters 81–93 in the common numbering), told by the sage Medhas to King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi.

es.stem: el Devi Mahatmya, también llamado Chandi o Durga Saptashati, ¿dentro de qué texto más amplio se encuentra tradicionalmente?
options: el Brahmanda Purana
el Markandeya Purana
el Bhagavata Purana
el Shiva Purana
es.why: El Devi Mahatmya es un bloque de trece capítulos del Markandeya Purana (capítulos 81–93 en la numeración común), que el sabio Medhas le cuenta al rey Suratha y al comerciante Samadhi.

stem: in the first episode of the Devi Mahatmya, Brahma is threatened by the demons Madhu and Kaitabha and praises the goddess as Yoganidra. why does he turn to her?
options: she created the two demons and alone can call them back
she is Brahma's own consort, sworn to protect the creator
Vishnu had asked her to keep watch over him while he slept
she is the sleep holding Vishnu, so only she can wake him
why: Devi Mahatmya 1: Vishnu lies in yogic sleep on the cosmic waters, and that sleep, Yoganidra, is the goddess. Brahma praises her so she will leave Vishnu's body and wake him; she does, and Vishnu kills the two demons.

es.stem: en el primer episodio del Devi Mahatmya, Brahma se ve amenazado por los demonios Madhu y Kaitabha y alaba a la diosa como Yoganidra. ¿por qué recurre a ella?
options: ella creó a los dos demonios y solo ella puede hacerlos volver
ella es la consorte de Brahma y juró proteger al creador
Vishnu le había pedido que lo cuidara mientras dormía
ella es el sueño de Vishnu y solo ella puede despertarlo
es.why: Devi Mahatmya 1: Vishnu yace en sueño yóguico sobre las aguas cósmicas, y ese sueño, Yoganidra, es la diosa. Brahma la alaba para que salga del cuerpo de Vishnu y lo despierte; así lo hace, y Vishnu mata a los dos demonios.

stem: in the Devi Mahatmya, Kali springs from the goddess's frowning brow and brings her the heads of the demons Chanda and Munda. what name does the goddess then give her?
options: Chamunda
Kaushiki
Shakambhari
Bhramari
why: Devi Mahatmya 7.25–27: because Kali has brought Chanda and Munda, the goddess says she will be known in the world as Chamunda.

es.stem: en el Devi Mahatmya, Kali brota de la frente fruncida de la diosa y le trae las cabezas de los demonios Chanda y Munda. ¿qué nombre le da entonces la diosa?
options: Chamunda
Kaushiki
Shakambhari
Bhramari
es.why: Devi Mahatmya 7.25–27: como Kali le ha traído a Chanda y a Munda, la diosa dice que será conocida en el mundo como Chamunda.

stem: in the Devi Mahatmya's last battle, the demon Shumbha taunts the goddess for fighting with the strength of others. what happens next in the text?
options: the gods take back the powers they had lent to her
Kali alone stays beside her while the rest withdraw
the goddesses enter her body, being her own powers
she sends the other goddesses back to their own gods
why: Devi Mahatmya 10.3–5: she answers that she alone exists in the world, and that the goddesses are her own powers; Brahmani and the others then enter her body, and she faces Shumbha alone.

es.stem: en la última batalla del Devi Mahatmya, el demonio Shumbha se burla de la diosa por pelear con la fuerza de otros. ¿qué pasa después en el texto?
options: los dioses recuperan los poderes que le habían prestado
solo Kali se queda a su lado y las demás se retiran
las diosas entran en ella, pues son sus propios poderes
ella devuelve las otras diosas a sus propios dioses
es.why: Devi Mahatmya 10.3–5: ella responde que solo ella existe en el mundo y que las diosas son sus propios poderes; Brahmani y las demás entran entonces en su cuerpo, y ella enfrenta sola a Shumbha.

stem: in Shaiva tradition, what does Ardhanarishvara, the form of Shiva whose body is half male and half female, chiefly express?
options: that Shiva and his Shakti are inseparable, never two
that Shiva and Vishnu share a single body, half each
that the goddess rules the world while Shiva meditates
that Shiva gave Parvati half his realm at their wedding
why: Ardhanarishvara, "the lord who is half woman," shows Shiva and Shakti, the god and his power, as one inseparable being; the Shiva Purana tells it as the form through which creation begins to multiply. (Shiva and Vishnu as one body is a different form, Harihara.)
source: Shiva Purana, Shatarudra Samhita 3; Kalidasa, Raghuvamsha 1.1

es.stem: en la tradición shivaíta, ¿qué expresa sobre todo Ardhanarishvara, la forma de Shiva cuyo cuerpo es mitad masculino y mitad femenino?
options: que Shiva y su Shakti son inseparables, nunca dos
que Shiva y Vishnu comparten un solo cuerpo, mitad y mitad
que la diosa gobierna el mundo mientras Shiva medita
que Shiva le dio a Parvati la mitad de su reino al casarse
es.why: Ardhanarishvara, "el señor que es mitad mujer", muestra a Shiva y Shakti, el dios y su poder, como un solo ser inseparable; el Shiva Purana lo cuenta como la forma por la que la creación empieza a multiplicarse. (Shiva y Vishnu en un solo cuerpo es otra forma, Harihara.)

stem: Shaiva and Shakta teachers speak of five acts of the divine (pancha-kritya), and the Lalita Sahasranama gives all five to the goddess. someone who for years saw only the ordinary world suddenly recognizes the divine within it. in this scheme, which act is at work?
options: srishti, creating
tirodhana, concealing
samhara, withdrawing
anugraha, grace
why: The five acts are creating, sustaining, withdrawing, concealing (tirodhana) and grace (anugraha). Concealing veils the divine so the world seems to be only itself; grace is the act that reveals it. Lalita Sahasranama 264–274 names the goddess as doer of all five.
source: Lalita Sahasranama 264–274; Shaiva Siddhanta and Kashmir Shaiva teaching on the five acts

es.stem: maestros shivaítas y shaktas hablan de cinco actos de lo divino (pancha-kritya), y el Lalita Sahasranama le atribuye los cinco a la diosa. alguien que durante años vio solo el mundo ordinario de pronto reconoce lo divino en él. en este esquema, ¿qué acto está obrando?
options: srishti, crear
tirodhana, ocultar
samhara, retirar
anugraha, gracia
es.why: Los cinco actos son crear, sostener, retirar, ocultar (tirodhana) y gracia (anugraha). Ocultar vela lo divino para que el mundo parezca ser solo él mismo; la gracia es el acto que lo revela. Lalita Sahasranama 264–274 nombra a la diosa como autora de los cinco.

stem: in Kashmir Shaivism, Vasugupta's Shiva Sutras open with "chaitanyam atma" (1.1) and "jnanam bandhah" (1.2). as Kshemaraja's commentary reads them, what do these two sutras say about the self and about bondage?
why: Shiva Sutras 1.1 says consciousness is the self: not something a person has, but what they are, and that consciousness is Shiva's own. 1.2 says knowledge is bondage, which Kshemaraja reads as limited knowing: taking oneself to be only this body and mind. Freedom is then a recognition (pratyabhijna), not a new acquisition.
source: Shiva Sutras 1.1–1.2; Kshemaraja, Shiva Sutra Vimarshini

rubric.point: says the self is consciousness itself (not something that merely has consciousness), and/or that this consciousness is Shiva's own, universal and free. "the self is aware" alone is partly met.
says the knowledge that binds is limited or contracted knowing: taking oneself to be only a limited body, mind or individual. saying that all learning or knowledge of scripture is bad does not count.
adds that freedom is a recognition of what one already is (pratyabhijna), not gaining something new.

es.stem: en el shivaísmo de Cachemira, los Shiva Sutras de Vasugupta comienzan con "chaitanyam atma" (1.1) y "jnanam bandhah" (1.2). según el comentario de Kshemaraja, ¿qué dicen estos dos sutras sobre el ser y sobre la atadura?
es.why: Shiva Sutras 1.1 dice que la conciencia es el ser: no algo que una persona tiene, sino lo que es, y esa conciencia es la de Shiva. 1.2 dice que el conocimiento es atadura, y Kshemaraja lo lee como conocer limitado: tomarse por solo este cuerpo y esta mente. La libertad es entonces un reconocimiento (pratyabhijna), no una adquisición nueva.

stem: in the classic South Indian bronze of Shiva as Nataraja, lord of the dance, what do the drum, the flame, the small figure under the planted foot and the raised foot stand for?
why: In the standard Shaiva reading (Unmai Vilakkam 36, made widely known by Ananda Coomaraswamy's The Dance of Shiva): the drum is creation, the flame is dissolution, the raised hand protects, the planted foot on Apasmara (Muyalakan) holds down ignorance, and the raised foot, to which the lower hand points, gives release.
source: Unmai Vilakkam 36; Ananda Coomaraswamy, The Dance of Shiva (1918)

rubric.point: the drum (damaru) stands for creation or the first sound, and the flame for dissolution or destruction. only one of the two correct is partly met.

the figure under the planted foot (Apasmara or Muyalakan) is ignorance or forgetfulness, held down; reading the planted foot as concealment (tirodhana) also counts. calling him simply "a demon" with no meaning is partly met.
the raised foot stands for release, grace or refuge (moksha, anugraha), often noting the lower hand that points to it.
mentions another element correctly: the raised right hand's gesture of protection ("do not fear"), the ring of fire as the cosmos, or the dance as the five acts of the divine.

es.stem: en el bronce clásico del sur de la India de Shiva como Nataraja, señor de la danza, ¿qué representan el tambor, la llama, la pequeña figura bajo el pie apoyado y el pie levantado?
es.why: En la lectura shivaíta clásica (Unmai Vilakkam 36, difundida por La danza de Shiva de Ananda Coomaraswamy): el tambor es la creación, la llama la disolución, la mano alzada protege, el pie apoyado sobre Apasmara (Muyalakan) mantiene abajo la ignorancia, y el pie levantado, al que apunta la mano inferior, da la liberación.
